neighbours.label: a farm-labour context at the point where a field or farm location is coming ('in the| fields', 'on the| farm'), as against the same sentence shapes set in non-agricultural places
fire: The pickers spent the whole August afternoon bent over in the fields.
Every spring the family hired extra hands to work on the farm.
After the harvest, the stubble was burned in the fields to clear them.
Old tractors were left rusting out in the field behind the barn.
The hired men were up at dawn to bring the cattle in from the pasture.
Much of the potato crop was left lying in the field after the rains.
As a boy he spent his summers helping his uncle bale hay on the farm.
The workers hoed weeds between the rows of corn in the hot sun.
quiet: The clerks spent the whole August afternoon bent over in the office.
Every spring the hotel hired extra staff to work at the front desk.
After the concert, the rubbish was cleared from the hall to tidy it.
Old computers were left gathering dust in the room behind the library.
The night nurses were up at dawn to bring the patients their breakfast.
Much of the paperwork was left lying on the desk after the meeting.
As a boy he spent his summers helping his uncle sell books in the city.
The students filed papers between the rows of shelves in the archive.
